## Summary

Copilot CLI v1.0.7 loads superpowers skills correctly from a plugin directory, but there is no working mechanism for a plugin to inject the "always check skills first" bootstrap context at session start.

## What works

- **Skills load perfectly** — all 19 superpowers skills are discovered and shown in `/skills`
- **Skill invocation works** — `skill(brainstorming)`, `skill(using-superpowers)` etc. all work

items.author: jfiscman
items.body:
## Feature Description

Make Superpowers skills available for **Hermes Agent** ([NousResearch/hermes-agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent)), an open-source autonomous agent framework by Nous Research.

Hermes is in the same category as OpenCode, Claude Code, and Codex — it has its own native skill system and runs on any LLM provider. Many users who run multiple coding agents would benefit from having Superpowers skills available in Hermes as well.

## Motivation

Hermes Agent has a mature built-in skill system (markdown files with YAML frontmatter, stored in `~/.hermes/skills/`)
items.title: Feature Request: Hermes Agent harness support — make Superpowers skills available in native Hermes format

# Feature request: opt-in mode that disables auto-triggering

## Problem

Installing Superpowers changes Claude Code's default behavior globally. The SessionStart hook injects the `using-superpowers` meta-skill into every session, mandating skill checks before any response. There's no way to keep skills available via slash commands while leaving Claude's default behavior intact. Users who want to evaluate Superpowers incrementally — or only use it for specific workflows — must manually edit `session-start` after each install/update.

## Proposal

Add a `SUPERPOWERS_MODE` environment variable c
items.title: Feature request: opt-in mode that disables auto-triggering
